commonName: Nguni / crossbred beef cattle (communal and extensive veld)

evidence.quote: Calves’ in humid zone had higher performance with 121.21 kg for WW, 96.83 kg for P-WG and 0.477 kg/day for P-ADG. The lowest WW (114.51 kg)...were observed in arid zone.
evidence.doc: Mpofu, Ginindza, Siwendu, Nephawe & Mtileni (2016). Effect of agro-ecological zone, season of birth and sex on pre-weaning performance of Nguni calves in Limpopo Province, South Africa. Tropical Animal Health and Production 49:187-194 (PMC5203849), Table 5

outputPerAnimal.notes: Table 5 gives weaning weight (WW) across four agro-ecological zones for the same nine Nguni communal herds: arid 114.51 kg (lowest), semi-arid 119.98 kg, dry sub-humid 117.91 kg, humid 121.21 kg (highest). The range recorded here spans this one study's own arid-to-humid zone means; it is not merged with any other paper's weaning-weight figures (other SA studies report different ranges for different systems - e.g. research-station or stud herds - and were deliberately excluded to avoid mixing systems). 826 Nguni calves from nine herds that the paper itself says were 'kept under extensive grazing system' in Limpopo Province - a genuine communal/extensive veld system matching this enterprise.

timeToFirstProductWeeks.notes: Withdrawn in editor review: 896.8 days is age at first calving, but a beef cow's product here is a weaned calf, which comes months after calving. No source states the time to a first weaned calf.

evidence.doc: Ngayo, M. (2017). Factors Affecting Productive Life and Fertility in Nguni Cows (MSc dissertation, University of the Free State), Table 5.1

productiveLifeYears.notes: 2354 days / 365.25 = 6.44 years. 'Failure time' is the length of productive herd life for the 580 uncensored (fully-observed) records in the combined dataset; the dissertation itself defines productive herd life as 'the time interval between first calving date to culling date'. Combined data from three extensively-grazed Nguni stud herds, animals born 1968-2015.

feedKgPerAnimalPerDay.notes: Not sourced for a breeding beef cow on extensive veld/communal grazing. Searches for ARC, SAJAS and LRRD cattle feed-intake figures found only intensive-feedlot, post-weaning-weaner ration studies (a different animal-stage and system from a mature breeding cow on veld) or sources that were unreachable (Springer full text redirected to a login page; sasas.co.za blocked by Cloudflare) within the search budget - see gaps.

waterLPerAnimalPerDay.notes: Not sourced for a beef cow on veld within the search budget - see gaps.

spaceM2PerAnimal.notes: Withdrawn in editor review: 1.74 m² is the handling and transport code's minimum for a holding pen, not space to keep a cow in. No source gives camp or housing space per beef cow.

welfare.point: Cattle pens must not be overcrowded: there must be enough floor space for every animal to lie down at the same time.

evidence.quote:
Livestock shall not be penned in overcrowded conditions. ... Penning space provided shall be enough to permit all livestock to lie down at the same 
time
evidence.doc: Livestock Welfare Coordinating Committee, Code of Practice: Handling and Transport of Livestock (2018), s.1.2

welfare.point: During transport, cattle must have at least 1.4 m² of floor space each so loading is neither too tight nor too loose.

evidence.doc: Livestock Welfare Coordinating Committee, Code of Practice: Handling and Transport of Livestock (2018), s.4.6.1

welfare.point: Cattle may not be transported for more than 18 hours without being off-loaded and given feed, water and shelter.

evidence.quote:
Livestock shall not be transported for periods in excess of 18 h. If the journey is longer than  
18 h the livestock shall be off-loaded and provided with suitable feed, potable water and shelter.
evidence.doc: Livestock Welfare Coordinating Committee, Code of Practice: Handling and Transport of Livestock (2018), s.7.1

welfare.point: It is an offence to starve, under-feed, or deny water or food to cattle.

evidence.quote: unnecessarily starves or under-feeds or denies water or food to any animal

legal.point: Foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) is a controlled animal disease under the Animal Diseases Act: state Veterinary Services enforce isolation and movement restrictions.

evidence.quote: FMD is classified as a controlled animal disease under the Animal Diseases Act, 1984 (Act No. 35 of 1984), which mandates specific control measures, such as isolation and movement restrictions, enforced by Veterinary Services.
evidence.doc: SAnews: KZN Foot and Mouth Disease boundaries extended (Dept of Agriculture statement)

legal.point: Every cattle owner must register an official identification mark and brand or mark their cattle with it, under the Animal Identification Act.

evidence.quote: Each owner of animals must- (a) apply for registration of an identification mark in terms of section 5 (1); (b) mark his or her animals in the prescribed manner

evidence.quote: all suspected and confirmed cases of abortion must be reported to the nearest State Veterinary office for zoo-sanitary actions as prescribed in the national bovine brucellosis control scheme
evidence.doc: Marumo, Hlokwe & Kayoka-Kabongo, Seroprevalence of brucellosis in communal and smallholder cattle farming in North West Province, South Africa, Onderstepoort Journal of Veterinary Research (PMC10784229)

gaps: outputPerAnimal: three different SA sources gave substantially different Nguni weaning-weight figures for different systems (a stud/research-station ecotype study; a Mpumalanga CPA report; this Limpopo communal-herd study). Only PMC5203849's own arid-to-humid zone range (114.51-121.21 kg) was used, since it is a single, clearly-extensive/communal-system source; the other figures were not merged in, per the instruction not to mix systems into one range.

timeToFirstProductWeeks and productiveLifeYears come from a registered-stud Nguni dissertation (Ngayo 2017, UFS), a different herd population from the communal Limpopo weaning-weight study. Both are extensively-grazed Nguni cattle on veld, but no single source covering a purely communal/smallholder herd gave both an age-at-first-calving and a productive-life figure together, so these two fields are not from the same document as outputPerAnimal (each field's value is still a single, undivided figure from one source, not stitched across documents).

feedKgPerAnimalPerDay and waterLPerAnimalPerDay: no SA-specific feed or water intake figure for a mature breeding beef cow on extensive veld/communal grazing was found. Available cattle feed/water studies (ARC, SAJAS, MDPI) covered intensive feedlot post-weaning weaners instead - a different animal-stage/system - so were excluded rather than mixed in. Some candidate sources (Springer full text, sasas.co.za) were unreachable (login redirect / Cloudflare block) within budget.

spaceM2PerAnimal: the only cattle-specific space figure found (LWCC Code, s.1.2.1) is a pre-transport holding-pen minimum, not routine extensive-veld camp space; no source was found quantifying typical grazing camp size per beef cow on communal land.

The LWCC 'Code of Practice for the Welfare of Dairy Cattle' PDF (a candidate welfare source) has an irrecoverably garbled custom font encoding under pypdf, pymupdf and WebFetch alike; abandoned in favour of the LWCC 'Code of Practice: Handling and Transport of Livestock' (2018), which extracts cleanly and is also an official, DAFF-linked, multi-organisation code applicable to cattle.

Editor review 2026-09-28 (round 2): productionMonths and seasonalPattern withdrawn. Mpofu et al. Table 2 defines the study's two birth seasons (summer Nov-Jan, winter May-Jul) for comparing calves; it does not say the herds calve only then, and calving is not when beef is taken. timeToFirstProductWeeks withdrawn (age at first calving, not a first weaned calf). spaceM2PerAnimal withdrawn (holding-pen minimum). The weaning-weight quote now carries the 121.21 kg humid-zone figure as well as the 114.51 kg arid one. PMC pages serve a reCAPTCHA to scripts, so PMC quotes were checked against the Europe PMC full text of the same articles.
